methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $75M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Sofar Ocean is a Series B-stage company operating in the ocean and maritime technology sector. The company has raised $75M+ to date. The valuation analysis is constrained by the absence of publicly traded comparables and identified private peers in the immediate comp universe, limiting triangulation to stage-based progression methodology.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $75M total capital raised as a proxy baseline. This method yields an implied valuation of $142M. The single-method approach produces a range anchored at $121M (low), $142M (median), and $164M (high), reflecting modest sensitivity analysis around the core 1.9x multiplier assumption.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $121M to $164M, with $142M as the central point estimate. Key limitations include reliance on a single methodological pillar—stage progression—and absence of sector-specific or peer-company calibration. Notably, no public or private comparables were identified to stress-test the step-up multiple or validate whether 1.9x reflects maritime-tech risk and growth profiles specifically. Resolution of these uncertainties would benefit from either identifying relevant ocean-tech or maritime infrastructure comparables, or obtaining forward-looking revenue and growth rate data to support revenue multiple or DCF approaches.
